ratings_why.fun: Four payoff axes (count, lump, live Debt, Ledger) share one number, so every Borrow, sale and Mr Magpie move is a real choice; the many '+1/+1 on Repaid' buffers keep it from an 8.
ratings_why.distinct: Earns 8 over 7 because Debt is one number that is a loan, a fight stat and a trigger source at once: you inflate it on purpose, read it at Start of Combat, then kill it down with Skims, which no tribe today does.

verdict_why: One real rules gap (does a free Skim repayment count as gold for the Ledger and Arne) needs a line; the rest is ready.

points.text: Say whether a Skim's free repayment, and Uncle Jack's sale repayment, count as gold repaid for the Ledger. The rulings say golden Skim counts for Arne's 'each 2 gold', but the Ledger only takes 'gold repaid', so Grandmother Corbie and Oast Bookkeeper read differently under Skim builds.

Because The Black Feather and Hooded Crow Heavy lock Debt at Start of Combat, Skimmers then pay it off at no cost to them, so the Racket and Debt-readers combine rather than clash. That is a lovely combo; say so in the builds instead of selling it as a tension.

Tower Raven's Borrow lands in reading order, so placing it before The Black Feather and Hooded Crow Heavy adds 4 to what they read. Make the slot-order puzzle visible on the board preview; it is the best positioning decision in the tribe.
Slate-Drinker Rook is only a Debt battery. A small rider that rewards keeping Debt into the fight (e.g. it gains Skim 1 while you have Debt) would give it a second use.
Grandmother Corbie only counts the Ledger. A twist tied to how the Ledger grew (e.g. extra for each repayment this turn) would let her reward the Racket or the Pawnshop, not just the steady line.

standouts.why: Uncle Jack turns any sale, any tribe, Created units included, into a repayment, so selling becomes a buff and mixes the tribe into everything.
Mr Magpie times the bill by board position: move him forward to call the lump in on the turn you choose.
Thought and Memory multiplies repayments, not stats, so it supercharges whichever build you picked, and its cap rule creates real choices with Corbie's Grandchick.

weakest.why: Slate-Drinker Rook is negative gold for Debt alone; it does one quiet job.
Grandmother Corbie is a plain counter-reading scaler at the top of a tribe full of tricks.
Silas Glint is two gold a fight with no decision attached.

flags.note: Tower Raven's 3 gold per fight is free whenever Skimmers clear its Debt; with The Belfry Mob and Silas Glint that is about 5 gold a fight.
Seven with The Belfry Mob and Tower Raven gives the tribe +1/+1 per Skim, up to the Debt, every fight, and the gold from Borrow stays free.
Arne with Thought and Memory and Uncle Jack gives the whole tribe +2/+2 per sale while in Debt; bounded by gold, but worth the owner's eye.
